## Refresh Token Lifetime and Re-auth

Access tokens last ~8 hours and are refreshed proactively by the background task (observed cadence: one successful `background token refresh succeeded` every ~7h45m). The **refresh token** itself also expires, and when it does the account is permanently `disabled` until a human re-auths — there is no auto-recovery path in the proxy.

Observed lifetimes (dated pod-log evidence; older rows retained as history):

| Provisioned / lineage | First `invalid_grant` (UTC) | Lifetime | Anthropic `error_description` |
|---|---|---|---|
| ~2026-06-20 | 2026-08-01 18:36Z | ~6 weeks | `Refresh token expired` |
| (earlier keychain grant) | 2026-06-20 02:12Z | — | `Refresh token not found or invalid` |
| 2026-08-26 / keychain, `claude-max-local` | 2026-09-23 07:26:55Z (inline refresh) | ~28 days | `Refresh token expired` |
| 2026-08-26 / PKCE, `claude-max-1787733199` | 2026-09-24 19:44:37Z (background refresh) | ~29.5 days | `Refresh token expired` |

Two distinct descriptions have been seen. `Refresh token expired` reads as a server-side TTL. `Refresh token not found or invalid` is more consistent with the token having been rotated away by another client (Anthropic rotates the refresh token on every successful refresh; the local Claude Code that the credential was extracted from refreshes the *same* grant independently). Neither cause is confirmed. The September failures at similar ages support a ~30-day server-side grant lifetime as an inference from timing and error text; they do not prove a fixed vendor TTL or that PKCE grants last longer than keychain grants.

Complete pool unavailability lasted from 2026-09-24 19:44:37Z to 2026-10-04 05:38:31Z (~9.4 days); this dates credential/pool unavailability, not a count of failed requests. See the [recovery audit](../audits/OAUTH_GRANT_EXPIRY_2026-10-04.md) for per-account evidence and client verification.

- Plan for re-auth on roughly a 30-day cycle per account, regardless of PKCE or keychain lineage, and arrange browser consent before the observed expiry window. This is an operational estimate, not a guaranteed lifetime. For the October 4 grant, ~2026-11-03 is the next planning window. - Symptom on the client side is `503 … "type":"pool_exhausted"` with `accounts_disabled ≥ 1` in the embedded pool summary ([Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md#pool-exhausted-oauth-mode)).
- Re-auth via [PKCE](#adding-an-account-pkce-flow): add the new account, confirm it is available in `/admin/pool`, then remove the disabled account by its exact ID. Verify `/health` body status and an end-to-end client request; a restart with the same credentials cannot restore an expired grant. Record the first rejection and its description before removing the old account.
- Until the account is replaced, the background task logs `refresh token rejected, disabling account` every 5 minutes for the already-disabled account (known noise — see [Known Issues](./troubleshooting.md#background-refresh-keeps-retrying-disabled-accounts)).

Propose shared rule: stop pinning CI-owned self-built images in Kustomize manifests
labels: 

## Summary

`default.json` extends `config:best-practices`, which includes `docker:pinDigests`. That rule pins every
`docker`-datasource dependency except those from the argocd, devcontainer, helmv3, and pyenv managers. A
repository whose CI writes its own image tag into a Kustomize manifest therefore receives a recurring
`pinDigest` PR that conflicts with CI and is reverted by CI on the next deploy.

This issue proposes a shared rule for that pattern. It does not select policy; the operator decides.

## Evidence

The affected consumer is `basher83/tailnet-microservices`:

- `k8s/kustomization.yaml` references `ghcr.io/basher83/tailnet-microservices/anthropic-oauth-proxy` with
  `newTag: sha-<commit>`.
- The `Update K8s Tag` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `sed -i "s/newTag: .*/newTag: ${SHA_TAG}/"` on every
  push to `main`. That replaces the whole line, including any `@sha256:` digest Renovate adds.
- Renovate has proposed the same pin repeatedly: #11 (merged), #45 (closed), and #51 (open, conflicting, and
  pinned to an April tag while `main` is on an October tag). Manual commit `73688d8` also pinned it once.
- Upstream `config:best-practices` extends `docker:pinDigests` (`lib/config/presets/internal/config.preset.ts`).
  `docker:pinDigests` exempts only argocd, devcontainer, helmv3, and pyenv, so kustomize is covered.
- No preset here exempts a repository's own CI-built images. The only `pinDigests` settings are `true` in
  `docker.json`, `kubernetes.json`, and `github-actions-security.json`, plus `false` in `python.json`.

## Consumer survey (blast radius)

Local checkouts under `~/3I` and GitHub code search across `basher83` found Renovate-visible manifests that
reference a `ghcr.io/basher83/*` image only in `tailnet-microservices`. Other hits are docs, incident records,
and `Zammad-MCP/scripts/docker-build.sh`, which builds an image that no surveyed manifest deploys.
`mothership-gitops` deploys the proxy by pointing ArgoCD at the `tailnet-microservices` kustomization, so it
has no image reference of its own. GHCR package listing was not checked because the token lacked
`read:packages`, and code search can miss unindexed files.

No current consumer deploys a `basher83`-built image from a different repository. A shared rule would not
suppress updates anywhere today.

## Local fix applied first

`tailnet-microservices/renovate.json` gets this rule:

```json
{
  "description": "CI's Update K8s Tag job owns the proxy image tag; Renovate must not pin or update it",
  "matchManagers": ["kustomize"],
  "matchPackageNames": ["ghcr.io/basher83/tailnet-microservices/**"],
  "enabled": false
}
```

Verification used Renovate 44.222.0 (`--platform=local --dry-run=lookup`) with the shared presets inlined as
`github>` references. Without the rule, 119 dependencies were extracted and the proxy image received
`pinDigest`. With the rule, the proxy image was `skipReason: disabled`, and the other 118 dependencies were
unchanged. `renovate-config-validator --strict` on 44.222.0 passed. The hosted app's resolution of `local>`
presets was not exercised.

## Proposal: shared rule

Add a kustomize-scoped rule to `default.json`, or make it an opt-in preset:

```json
{
  "description": "Do not pin or update basher83-built images in Kustomize manifests; consumer CI owns those tags",
  "matchManagers": ["kustomize"],
  "matchPackageNames": ["ghcr.io/basher83/**"],
  "enabled": false
}
```

The operator needs to decide the following:

1. Should this go in `default.json` (implicit for every consumer) or in an opt-in preset such as
   `presets/self-built-images.json`? With one known consumer, `default.json` placement needs an explicit operator
   exception to the representative-consumer-evidence requirement.
2. Should the rule use `enabled: false` or `pinDigests: false`? `enabled: false` also stops tag updates. That is
   correct for CI-owned `sha-*` tags but wrong if a future GitOps repository deploys a released `ghcr.io/basher83/*`
   image built elsewhere.
3. As an alternative, consumer CI could write `newTag: sha-<commit>@sha256:<build digest>` and keep the
   `best-practices` digest intent without a Renovate exemption.

## Related finding: unpinned validator version

The `validate-renovate-root` and `validate-renovate-presets` tasks in `mise.toml` run
`npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator`. With no version specified, `npx` reuses whatever
is cached, which is Renovate 37.440.7 on the operator workstation. Renovate 37 matches only exact names in
`matchPackageNames` and `matchDepNames`; glob and regex support arrived in v38. During this investigation, the
cached v37 made glob rules appear not to match. The validation gate may therefore check presets against a much
older schema and matcher than the hosted app runs. This deserves a separate decision on pinning the version,
for example `renovate@<version>` managed by Renovate itself.

The local rule is right and the facts in the issue check out. My main concern is that the issue's title and framing argue for a shared rule, which is the opposite of your position.

**The `renovate.json` rule:** no concerns.
- It's limited to the `kustomize` manager and this repo's image path, and `enabled: false` is right because CI owns the tag completely, not just the digest.
- Your dry-run on Renovate 44.222.0 is good evidence: the proxy image showed `skipReason: disabled` and the other 118 dependencies were unchanged. The `**` pattern needs Renovate 38 or later, which the hosted app has. Your own note applies: the hosted app's lookup of the shared presets wasn't exercised, so the first real Renovate run is the actual confirmation.
- It's still uncommitted. Once it's on `main`, I'd close #51 by hand and not wait to see whether Renovate closes it.

**Evidence in #135:** I checked it.
- #11 was merged on 2026-04-28 and pinned to `a1c4f12`.
- #45 was closed unmerged on 2026-05-19.
- `73688d8` ("deploy: pin current image digest", 2026-04-28) changed only `k8s/kustomization.yaml`.
- So the same pin has been proposed three times and reverted by CI each time. That's a stronger case than I made earlier.

**Concerns with #135:**

1. **The title and structure contradict your position.** The issue is titled "Propose shared rule…" and its main section is "Proposal: shared rule" with a `ghcr.io/basher83/**` rule ready to paste in. The body says it "does not select policy", but anyone skimming will read it as asking for a shared exclusion. Your own survey argues against one: there's one consumer, and no `basher83` image is deployed from a different repo. I'd retitle it along the lines of "CI-owned image tags: handled per repo; record why no shared rule". Lead with the local fix as the decision, and keep the shared rule as an alternative that was considered and rejected, along with what would change that (a second repo whose CI owns its image tag).

2. **Option 3 is the most useful idea in the issue, and it's mostly a change in this repo, not in renovate-config.** If CI wrote the image's digest along with the tag, every deploy would point at an exact, unchangeable image. Two notes if you pursue it:
   - Kustomize has its own `digest:` field, and `kustomize edit set image name:tag@sha256:…` writes it properly. The `ci.yml:126` sed only rewrites `newTag:`, so adding a digest by hand would leave a stale one behind.
   - The Docker job would need to output the image digest so the deploy job can use it. `docker/build-push-action` provides that as an output.

   It deserves its own issue in this repo if you want it, not a footnote in a renovate-config issue.

3. **Split the unpinned validator into its own issue.** It's a real gap in renovate-config: the validation gate can run Renovate 37 while the hosted app runs 44, and you saw v37 get the `**` pattern wrong. It's unrelated to image pinning, so it will get lost if it stays as a trailing section of #135.

4. **The decision questions are mostly answered already.** Questions 1 and 2 (`default.json` or an opt-in preset, `enabled` or `pinDigests`) only matter if a shared rule is wanted. If the decision is per-repo, both are moot, and `enabled: false` is right for the local rule. Leaving them open invites a decision nobody needs to make.

cat > "$TMPDIR/issue.md" <<'EOF'
## Summary

Have CI deploy the proxy by image digest, not just by the mutable-in-principle `sha-<commit>` tag. The `Update K8s Tag` job would write both the tag and the build digest into `k8s/kustomization.yaml`, so ArgoCD deploys exactly the image the Docker job pushed.

This is the in-repo follow-up to option 3 in basher83/renovate-config#135. Renovate is already disabled for this image (7670b5c), so this is about deploy immutability, not about Renovate.

## Current state

- `k8s/kustomization.yaml` has `images[0].newTag: sha-<commit>` and no `digest`.
- The `Docker` job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) builds with `docker/build-push-action` but the step has no `id` and the job declares no `outputs`, so the digest isn't available downstream.
- The `Update K8s Tag` job rewrites the tag with `sed -i "s/newTag: .*/newTag: ${SHA_TAG}/" kustomization.yaml`.

## Proposed change

1. Give the build step an `id` (e.g. `build`) and expose `steps.build.outputs.digest` as a job output of `docker`.
2. In `deploy`, replace the `sed` with `kustomize edit set image ghcr.io/basher83/tailnet-microservices/anthropic-oauth-proxy:${SHA_TAG}@${DIGEST}`, which writes Kustomize's separate `digest:` field. Do not hand-append `@sha256:` to `newTag`: the current `sed` only touches `newTag:` and would leave a stale `digest:` line behind.
3. Fail the deploy job if the digest output is empty, rather than committing a tag-only reference.

## Acceptance

- After a push to `main`, `k8s/kustomization.yaml` contains `newTag: sha-<commit>` and `digest: sha256:<…>` matching the pushed image in GHCR.
- `mise run k8s:validate` passes and the rendered Deployment image is `…@sha256:<digest>`.
- ArgoCD syncs and `mise run live:validate` passes.
- The runbook deployment doc (`docs/runbook/deployment.md`) describes the digest pin and how to roll back.

## Notes

- `kustomize` must be available on the runner (it's bundled in `kubectl kustomize`, but `kustomize edit` needs the standalone binary or an action).
- Main CI is currently blocked by the Audit job (11 RustSEC advisories in quinn-proto, rustls, rustls-webpki, webpki-root-certs), so Docker and deploy are skipped until that's fixed. That has to land first to verify this end to end.
EOF
